claims.text: Chemical short-range order suppresses lattice thermal conductivity in concentrated refractory high-entropy alloys relative to a disordered solid solution.
MoNbTaW is a body-centered-cubic refractory high-entropy alloy.
MoNbTaW has a significant energetic driving force for chemical short-range ordering.
Quenching MoNbTaW from above its ordering temperature produces a fully disordered solid-solution baseline.
Aging at 0.4–0.6 Tm induces SRO without causing long-range phase separation or precipitation.
SRO in the bcc lattice consists of non-random nearest-neighbor correlations.
Mo-Ta or Nb-W pairs are representative SRO pairings in MoNbTaW-like RHEAs.
SRO clusters create local potential-energy fluctuations.
Lattice thermal conductivity in concentrated solid solutions is dominated by phonon scattering from mass disorder and strain-field fluctuations.
SRO creates bond-stiffness and atomic-mass-distribution variations that are more pronounced than those of a random alloy.
SRO supplies an additional scattering mechanism for mid-to-high-frequency phonons.
SRO increases the phonon scattering rate and reduces the phonon mean free path.
SRO can reduce local mass variance.
In RHEAs, dispersion disruption and chemical scattering from SRO dominate over any transport enhancement caused by reduced local mass variance.
An SRO-containing aged sample will have 10–25% lower lattice thermal conductivity than the disordered sample over 300–1000 K.
The conductivity reduction will be greatest at 400–800 K because defect scattering is more important relative to phonon-phonon scattering there.
The proposed suppression mechanism applies only when the RHEA remains single-phase and bcc while developing SRO.
Long-range ordering or precipitation shifts the dominant mechanism to grain-boundary and phase-boundary scattering.
The strength and correlation length of SRO depend on the elemental pairings in the alloy.
The temperature dependence of SRO-induced conductivity suppression may vary when the SRO formation range overlaps strong Umklapp scattering.
